analysis:
Test-only changes; I found no security regression in the supplied units.

1) SSDShorterCheckpointRestoreTests.swift head 307-354: the same-ID replacement test now adds a second gate (replacementGate, head 330). The base test expected the replacement to queue behind the old read's exact-file lease (base 333-334, pendingCount == 1). The head test instead expects the old and replacement reads of the 512 file to proceed concurrently: pendingCount == 0 (head 342). It also asserts that the old attempt's unwind leaves the replacement's registration in store.reading intact (head 345). This suggests production SSDHybridCheckpointStore file-lease semantics changed from exclusive to shared reads. That production source is not in this batch. Integration should verify that shared read leases still exclude concurrent eviction, retire and corrupt-delete on the same file. It should also confirm the stale-attempt fences still hold (complete, close, epoch, cancel). These fences relate to T-041's staging-reservation release paths and authenticated-only staging.

2) SSDWholeRootTelemetryConcurrencyTests.swift head 17: the test double's retireOwnedEntries gains an unusedSince: Int64? parameter. This implies the SSDEvictableStore protocol changed so that TTL retirement is conditioned on last use. Integration should check how production stores use unusedSince. A sliding hit after the sweep's snapshot must prevent deletion, and nil must not bypass TTL expiry. The 30-minute TTL and LRU bounds in T-041/SEC-035 must not be extended.

The test double ignores unusedSince, which is acceptable for a mock. Neither change alters crypto, HMAC naming, salt scoping or AAD.
